claim: Starting from a smooth bell (Gaussian or cosine bump) instead of the constant and then hill-climbing on the heights raises R from the constant's 2/3 to about 0.79-0.80; the best single run reached 0.7952 with a Gaussian seed (s in 15-30) plus multiplicative hill-climbing on N=200, and a cosine-bump multi-stage search reached 0.8328.

A cosine-bump start with coordinate ascent and perturbed restarts (N=50) gave the generation's best score, 0.8328 (+0.1662 over the constant), with 24% of heights zero and a fatter f*f top (16.8% of knots within 0.1% of the max vs 2.7% for the Gaussian-seeded run).

Generalized Gaussian exp(-|x|^p) scanned over p=1.0-3.0 with scale variants and hill-climbing only reached 0.7933, below the plain Gaussian-seeded run's 0.7952; no p away from 2 gave a clear gain, so the p-family did not beat the Gaussian.

Smoothed-box seeds (erf-based, a in 0-2.0, w in 0.15-1.2) plus hill-climbing reached only 0.7875, the weakest of the three deep runs; the flat-topped family did not push f*f closer to a plateau than the Gaussian.

Does the win come from the seed shape or from the search? The cosine-bump run (p0004) beat the Gaussian-seeded run (p0005) at much coarser N (50 vs 200) with 24% zeros, suggesting a compact, partly-zero support may help; worth testing cosine-bump seeds at several N with the same hill-climber to separate seed from search.

Very fine grids did not help: N=3200 with progressive upsampling scored 0.7449 and N=800 with block hill-climbing scored 0.7863, both below the N=50 cosine-bump run's 0.8328; whether coarse N (50-200) is genuinely better than fine N under a fixed budget is worth a controlled test.

Upsampling p0004's N=50 asymmetric heights to N=100 via linear interpolation and re-polishing (coordinate ascent + perturbed restarts) raised R from 0.832821 to 0.833771 (+0.00095), the best score so far; the f*f peak moved from 0.390 to 0.545 of the support and ||f*f||_inf dropped from 1.1475 to 1.1436 while ||f*f||_2^2 stayed ~0.9535, so finer structure does help slightly at N=100.

Replacing p0004's single-index perturbation stage with full coordinate ascent (halving step) plus block/ramp perturbations at the same N=50 gave +0.000001 (0.832821 -> 0.832822): the N=50 optimum was already locally saturated, so block/segment moves found nothing new at that resolution.

Resampling the Gaussian-seeded N=200 solution to N=800 before multiplicative single-coordinate hill-climbing gave exactly 0.795235 (no change) and the output stayed at N=200 with 0% zeros and a symmetric f*f peak at 0.487; finer grid alone does not move the Gaussian line, consistent with F6 that fine grids don't help.

Cyclic coordinate ascent with multiplicative+additive moves, progressive upsampling and block-noise restarts on the N=3200 line raised R from 0.744910 to 0.759601 (+0.01469) but still stayed well below the coarse-N asymmetric runs (0.83); the f*f top remained sharp (2.09% of knots within 0.1% of max) and 0% zeros, so fine-grid search improves its own baseline without reaching the coarse-N regime.

The N=50 basin is exhausted regardless of search schedule.

Fine-N smooth-seeded search remains far below the coarse-N asymmetric/box line (0.848).

Replacing the exact max in the gradient by an annealed log-sum-exp softmax (spreading correction over near-max knots instead of only the argmax) plus the exact PGD and perturbation loop raised R from 0.868524 to 0.870986 (+0.0025); the f*f top got markedly flatter (0.1%-of-max knot share 15.8% -> 33.8%), confirming the myopic-max diagnosis.

Building a flat f*f directly from a sparse spike train (K=30 annealed spike centers chosen to flatten the pairwise-sum histogram, then PGD polish) scored only 0.657833, below the constant's 0.666667: 96.5% zeros, max/mean 36.2, and only 2.5% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max. The flat-histogram construction did not survive the polish and is not a viable route at this budget.

Replacing p0019's Powell/coordinate box search with exact-gradient ascent plus coordinate ascent and perturb-restart lost ground: R fell from 0.848602 to 0.847022 (-0.0016) at N=200 with only 2.0% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max. Gradient ascent alone is a weaker local search than Powell on the box-parameter family.

Pushing the PGD line to higher resolution (stages up to N=2000 with PGD, coordinate polish, small-noise perturbations) gained only +0.000369 (0.868524 -> 0.868893) and the peak drifted to 0.449 with 10.0% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max; fine grids still do not beat the coarse-N asymmetric basin.

An upsampling-to-N=400 PGD program with sinusoidal perturbations and an N=1200 final refinement crashed with 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (200,) (400,)': the sinusoidal perturbation was added to a length-200 array using a length-400 index. Mixing arrays of different N in the perturbation stage is a recurring crash mode.

Giving the box-compressed line (p0022, 0.865848) p0031's full-budget 7-move + exact-PGD loop at N=400 with N=800 probes gained only +0.00021 (0.865848 -> 0.866059), leaving it ~0.0075 below p0031's 0.8725; the two families did not converge, so the box line's deficit is structural, not a search-budget artifact.

Adding multi-resolution PGD (N up to 1200), smoothed-noise perturbations and a best-restart schedule to the box line (p0022, 0.865848) gained only +0.00003 (0.865881) at N=1200 with 24.2% zeros and a peak at 0.444; finer grids and richer perturbations do not lift the box family, consistent with the coarse-N basin being locally saturated.
